title: Coinduction and its specified unit for quasi-coherent groupoid modules
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $(U,R,s,t,c,e,i)$ a groupoid in schemes over $S$ [def-a1-scheme-groupoid-laws]. Let $\mathcal C$ have objects $(M,\beta)$, where $M$ is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_U$-module [pqf-def-coherent], $\beta:t^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}s^*M$ [def-pc-module-pullback], $e^*\beta=1$, and $c^*\beta=\operatorname{pr}_1^*\beta\circ\operatorname{pr}_0^*\beta$ under the canonical pullback identifications. Its morphisms $f:(M,\beta)\to(N,\gamma)$ satisfy $s^*f\circ\beta=\gamma\circ t^*f$. Write $V:\mathcal C\to\operatorname{QCoh}(U)$ for the forgetful functor. Assume $s,t$ are flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], quasi-compact (inverse images of affine opens are quasi-compact) and quasi-separated (their diagonals are quasi-compact). There is a functor $G:\operatorname{QCoh}(U)\to\mathcal C$, with underlying object $VG(H)=s_*t^*H$ and underlying map $VG(h)=s_*t^*h$, right adjoint to $V$. The equivariant structure on $G(H)$ is natural in $H$. The underlying map of the unit $\eta_{(M,\beta)}:(M,\beta)\to G(M)$ is the composite $M\to s_*s^*M\xrightarrow{s_*(\beta^{-1})}s_*t^*M$, whose first arrow is the ordinary pullback-pushforward adjunction unit.

source.place: Tag 07TR (lemma-construct-quasi-coherent), and Tag 0GNF (remark-adjunction-map), including its explicit unit formula.

proof.text: Put $Q=R\times_{t,U,t}R$ with projections $q_0,q_1$. The pair groupoid $\mathcal P$ on $R$ has source $q_1$, target $q_0$, identity $a\mapsto(a,a)$, inverse $(a,b)\mapsto(b,a)$, and composition $((a,b),(b,z))\mapsto(a,z)$. These are scheme morphisms by the fibre-product universal property, and the groupoid identities are the displayed coordinate identities. Define $f:\mathcal P\to\mathcal R$ by $f_0=s$ and $f_1=d$, where $d(a,b)=a^{-1}b$. Its endpoints are $s(d(a,b))=s(b)$ and $t(d(a,b))=s(a)$; it preserves identity and inverse, and $d(a,b)d(b,z)=a^{-1}bb^{-1}z=a^{-1}z=d(a,z)$. Its target square is Cartesian: the mutually inverse morphisms $Q\rightleftarrows R\times_{s,U,t}R$ are $(a,b)\mapsto(a,a^{-1}b)$ and $(a,r)\mapsto(a,ar)$, compatible with $q_0$ and the first projection. The inverse identities follow from associativity and the inverse laws. All formulas hold naturally on every test scheme, and their composites are identities by the fibre-product universal property.

source.place: Tag 07TR, second paragraph; Tags 0233 (lemma-equivalence-groupoid) and 03C6 (lemma-diagram-pull), explicit coordinate verifications

proof.text: Since $te=1_U$, $t$ is surjective on points. For every affine open $W\subset U$, the quasi-compact scheme $t^{-1}W$ has a finite affine open cover whose images cover $W$. Together with flatness of $t$, this is precisely the definition of the singleton fpqc covering $\{t:R\to U\}$. Apply fpqc descent to obtain an equivalence $E:\operatorname{QCoh}(U)\to\operatorname{QCoh}(\mathcal P)$, $H\mapsto(t^*H,\mathrm{can})$. Here $\mathrm{can}:q_0^*t^*H\to q_1^*t^*H$ is the identification from $tq_0=tq_1$. The descent-data orientation is exactly target $q_0$ to source $q_1$; its cocycle is the pair-groupoid cocycle. The equivalence includes full faithfulness on all quasi-coherent modules, not only invertible ones.

source.place: Tag 07TR, second paragraph, invoking Descent Tag 023T (proposition-fpqc-descent-quasi-coherent)

proof.text:
For $(M,\beta)\in\mathcal C$, the pullback $f^*(M,\beta)$ has underlying module $s^*M$ and datum $d^*\beta$. Pull the given cocycle for $\beta$ back along $Q\to R\times_{s,U,t}R$, $(a,b)\mapsto(a,d(a,b))$. Since $ad(a,b)=b$, it reads $q_1^*\beta=d^*\beta\circ q_0^*\beta$, with the canonical identification of their $t^*M$ sources. Thus
$$d^*\beta=q_1^*\beta\circ\mathrm{can}\circ(q_0^*\beta)^{-1}.$$
Consequently $\beta:t^*M\to s^*M$ is an isomorphism $E(V(M,\beta))\xrightarrow{\sim}f^*(M,\beta)$ of descent data. For a morphism $a:(M,\beta)\to(N,\gamma)$ the defining equality $s^*a\circ\beta=\gamma\circ t^*a$ is exactly naturality of this isomorphism. This establishes a natural isomorphism $EV\cong f^*$ with its underlying map specified, rather than only an unspecified identification of functors.

source.place: Tag 07TR, final paragraph, pullback of the cocycle along (pr_0,c(i,1))

proof.text:
Apply the Cartesian groupoid adjunction to $f$. Its object map is the given qcqs morphism $s$; its target source and target maps are the given flat maps $s,t$; its target square is Cartesian by step 1. Set $G=f_*E$. This constructs its equivariant structures and their naturality, with underlying objects and maps exactly $s_*t^*H$ and $s_*t^*h$, and proves that they are quasi-coherent. The adjunction and the isomorphism of step 3 give the natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}((M,\beta),G(H))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{QCoh}(\mathcal P)}(f^*(M,\beta),E(H))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{QCoh}(\mathcal P)}(E(M),E(H))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{QCoh}(U)}(M,H).$$
The middle bijection is precomposition by $\beta$, and the last is the full faithfulness of $E$. Their inverse sends $h:M\to H$ to the ordinary $s^*\dashv s_*$ transpose of $t^*h\circ\beta^{-1}:s^*M\to t^*H$: after precomposition by $\beta$ this is precisely $t^*h$. Each constituent bijection is natural, so this specifies $V\dashv G$.

source.place: Tag 07TR, last two paragraphs; Tag 09VH (lemma-pushforward) and Descent Tag 023T

proof.text:
The unit at $(M,\beta)$ is the image of $1_M$ under the inverse Hom bijection in step 4. Since $t^*1_M=1_{t^*M}$, it is the ordinary transpose of $\beta^{-1}:s^*M\to t^*M$. By the unit formula for ordinary adjunction, that transpose is
$$M\xrightarrow{\eta^s_M}s_*s^*M\xrightarrow{s_*(\beta^{-1})}s_*t^*M.$$
It is equivariant because it was obtained from the restricted adjunction, and its naturality is the naturality of the constructed Hom bijections. This is exactly the specified unit of the item and Tag 0GNF.
